stage: Step 1 eligibility and initial alignment boundaries

scope.navigation_exposure_disclosure: An initial navigation dump included the complete agent_test/verifier blocks of screening_plan.json, including nested helper annotations such as reference_pass_risk and selection_correction. Later navigation was restricted to paths, test names, and trajectory step IDs. No top-level classification, step2, outcome, baseline_observation, summary, or reviewer_B files were read. The findings below were independently checked against instructions, original tests, implementation patches, trajectories, official tests/solution patches, and raw execution output. This review should not be described as perfectly blinded because of the initial nested-annotation exposure.
scope.interpretation: A passing agent test on the reference is not required to establish Step 1. It is required, together with delivered PASS, for the later original-t PASS/PASS contrast. No context-recoverable validation miss or masking/bypass success is certified at this stage.
scope.source_resolution: Original input_directory, task_directory, and archived_verifier_directory are resolved by screen_id from screening_order.json. All cases/... and screening/... paths below are relative to this run. Instruction/model.patch/trajectory and official tests/test.patch/solution/solution.patch refer to those original identity directories.
scope.population_inference: These candidates are a screened sample, not an estimate of population incidence.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: instruction.md requires explicit aliases equal to their own primary key to error at creation, but does not name an exception class. model.patch:496-501 raises ValueError for exactly this condition. tests/test.patch:304-313 instead requires ProviderNotFoundError from get_loader. That narrower exception-class contract is not independently established by the supplied task text.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: The original test_explicit_alias_equal_to_primary_key_errors exercises Retort/name_mapping/get_loader with an own-primary alias and expects ValueError. Trajectory step 209 reports 14 passed and step 218 reports 2834 passed, 28 skipped; this is a genuinely executed related validation, not a missing test.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: Archived test-stdout.txt:51-131 contains an executed test_alias_same_as_own_primary_key failure with ValueError; the summary reports 1 failed, 43 passed. It is an observed exception mismatch, but its status as a task violation remains unresolved.

reference_support.evidence: Official solution.patch:586-627 accumulates CannotProvide errors and raises AggregateCannotProvide, consistent with the official ProviderNotFoundError expectation. No fresh reference execution for this candidate was available in cases/S001/baseline. The reference's implementation choice alone does not establish a missing task-level exception contract.

notes: Do not count a confirmed validation miss solely because the official verifier asks for a different exception subclass.

Needed evidence: a pre-existing documented public get_loader exception contract or another task-supported behavioral defect. More runs showing the same class mismatch will not resolve this semantic gap.
Changing pytest.raises(ValueError) to ProviderNotFoundError would change the assertion, not setup.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The contract requires creation-time errors for own-primary and cross-field collisions but does not specify ProviderNotFoundError or require deferral specifically to get_loader. model.patch:182-193 raises ValueError during name_mapping for statically visible collisions; the official own-primary test builds the recipe outside its raises block. Both exception class and exact creation stage are stricter than the explicit task text.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: test_explicit_alias_equal_to_own_primary_key_raises wraps the recipe and get_loader expression in pytest.raises(ValueError, match='equals its own primary key'). Trajectory step 180 reports 25 passed and step 194 reports 2851 passed, 28 skipped.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: Archived test-stdout.txt:245-332 shows execution failing at name_mapping with ValueError, before the verifier's expected get_loader exception context. Four collision tests fail; 40 pass. This is runtime evidence, not compilation/collection failure.

reference_support.evidence: Official solution uses CannotProvide/AggregateCannotProvide during alias layout creation and official tests require ProviderNotFoundError. Fresh P/R executions are absent; the reference does not by itself justify this stronger public contract.

notes: Needed evidence: an independent exception-type and creation-stage contract, or another clear task violation.
Do not interpret the earlier ValueError as failure to reject the invalid configuration; it does reject it.
Later context work cannot fix a frozen ValueError assertion by replacing its exception class.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: instruction.md specifies creation errors but no exact class. model.patch:522-526 and 820-828 implement/test ValueError for own-primary and cross-field aliases. Official tests demand ProviderNotFoundError. The observed discrepancy is not yet an independently grounded task defect.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: test_aliases_validation_errors invokes get_loader for own-primary, other-primary, and shared-alias collisions under three ValueError assertions. Trajectory step 173 reports 13 passed and step 179 reports 2874 passed, 28 skipped.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: Archived test-stdout.txt:213-287 shows the own-primary test reaching layout construction and raising ValueError. Four collision tests fail and 40 pass; these are executed runtime mismatches.

reference_support.evidence: The official alias solution statically supports its ProviderNotFoundError convention via CannotProvide aggregation. No fresh reference baseline exists for S003. This does not settle whether ValueError violates the original request.

notes: The original agent test and official test occupy the same original path; preserve original code identity when running either.
Needed evidence is the missing public exception contract, not just repeated official failure.
Assertion replacement would be assertion repair, not setup-only recovery.

Read consistently, save/list are route suffixes, supporting /api/snapshot/save and /api/snapshot/list. model.patch:932-937 instead installs POST/GET /api/snapshot/. Trajectory steps 55 and 101 show successful HTTP/JSON execution, and fresh agent_delivered/repeat_01 does likewise. HTTP statuses are printed rather than asserted; the implicit JSON/indexing checks still execute.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: cases/S004/baseline/verifier_delivered/repeat_01/steps/012_target/stdout.txt reproduces test_webui_snapshot_save: POST /api/snapshot/save returns 404 instead of 200.

reference_support.evidence: verifier_reference/repeat_01/steps/012_target/stdout.txt reports 1 passed. The original HTTP agent script fails on reference at its different POST /api/snapshot/ URL with ContentTypeError after HTTP 404; see agent_reference/repeat_01/steps/009_target/stderr.txt.

notes: The route notation is compact; the pass judgment uses the uniform named-operation reading, not reference success alone.
The original t is P PASS / R FAIL. This does not negate Step 1 but prevents a context-recovery success with this frozen original t.
Changing /api/snapshot/ to /api/snapshot/save changes the HTTP target input and is Different Stimulus Required, not setup-only recovery.
No additional execution evidence is needed to establish the currently observed URL discrepancy.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The instruction explicitly forbids a default on a variadic parameter and requires parse error 'invalid default argument declaration'. Official tests/test.patch:124-125 includes func a(b = 1, c... = 2) { return c }. The delivered verifier reports generic 'syntax error' instead of that required error.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: screening/S006/agent_test_selected_entry.go retains the exact original table entry func f(a = 1, b = 2...) {} with ParseError fmt.Errorf('invalid default argument declaration'). It appears in original authored trajectory step 117; the corrected containing test passes at steps 118, 174 and 179. Fresh agent_selected_entry_delivered and agent_selected_entry_reference both report PASS.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: cases/S006/baseline/verifier_delivered/repeat_01/steps/014_target/stdout.txt contains the executed TestDefaultArgumentsVisible failure: received syntax error, expected substring invalid default argument declaration. The model scanner explicitly handles default expressions ending in '...' at model.patch:439-442.

reference_support.evidence: verifier_reference/repeat_01/steps/014_target/stdout.txt passes. The selected entry passes on both implementations. The whole original TestDefaultArguments fails on reference for unrelated excess-argument/toString and nested-function-default cases; those are preserved separate observations.

notes: The independent table-entry projection is a defensible original t only when declared as the experimental unit and its Script/ParseError remain exact. It must not be represented as the complete original function.

The agent stimulus places '...' after the default expression; the official failing stimulus places it on the parameter before '='. Moving it in the selected Script would change input and require Different Stimulus Required.
The original selected entry satisfies P/R PASS/PASS; this alone is not a successful context intervention.
For precise attribution of the official aggregate failure, a raw per-entry verifier trace would be useful, although the clear contract and executed failure already establish Step 1.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The typed-binding behavior contract is explicit, but the supplied official run does not identify an executed runtime behavior violation. Its VM test binary fails to build.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: Trajectory step 81 authors TestTypedBindingsBasic and shows that specific test PASS; step 82 reports the typed-binding suite passing after other tests are corrected, and step 190 reports the full Go suite passing.

reference_support.evidence: No fresh P/R baseline is available. Reference source alone cannot turn this delivered build failure into a behavioral contrast.

notes: Needed evidence for reconsideration: the compiler diagnostic and an unchanged official behavioral verifier that actually executes against the submitted patch. Do not classify missing test results as behavioral FAIL.
This exclusion is limited to the supplied candidate evidence; it does not establish that the patch has no behavioral bugs.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The task explicitly requires compliance routes under /environments/:id/compliance and wiring in router_bootstrap.go. model.patch:38-41 passes apiGroup.Group('/environments') into RegisterRoutes, while model.patch:94-96 adds '/environments/:id/compliance' again. The resulting doubled prefix violates the requested public path.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: The original TestComplianceRoutes authors a real Gin router and exercises all compliance APIs, but its setup directly calls RegisterRoutes(router.Group('/api')). Trajectory step 115 reports PASS and step 148 reconfirms the selected suite. Fresh agent_delivered repeats 01 and 02 both pass.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: Archived TestWiring_SetupRouterRegistersDriftRoutes executes setupRouter and reports every required route missing. Fresh verifier_delivered repeats 01 and 02 under steps/014_target/stdout.txt reproduce those route assertions, not a build failure.

reference_support.evidence: Fresh verifier_reference repeats 01 and 02 pass and list correctly formed /api/environments/:id/compliance routes. The original full agent test fails on reference at its final missing-drift ignore request: expected 404, actual 200; agent_reference/repeat_01 and repeat_02/steps/009_target/stdout.txt.

notes: Fresh baselines arrived during this review and supersede the initial missing-evidence concern for S008.
The complete selected TestComplianceRoutes is P PASS / R FAIL because of its final ignore-missing assertion, so it does not meet the later original-t PASS/PASS rule.

Router construction is a plausible setup boundary for the fixed HTTP requests. However, replacing direct registration with setupRouter must not change request paths, bodies, assertions, or production code.

Deleting the unrelated final assertion after observing reference failure would change the selected t. Any smaller unit needs independent justification and a disclosed new selection; it cannot silently replace this full function.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The instruction requires recursive local $ref and specifically warns about recursive references inside anyOf. Official tests/test.patch:198-243 constructs a valid Tree containing recursive child/null branches and asserts that a valid nested value is accepted. The delivered result is false.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: screening/S009/agent_selected.test.ts exercises recursive $ref inside anyOf with an allOf object branch, accepting valid null/tree inputs and rejecting a wrong value type. Trajectory step 149 explicitly reports this test passing; step 186 reports 58 passing. Fresh agent_delivered/repeat_01_retry_02 reports 1 passing.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: cases/S009/baseline/verifier_delivered/repeat_01/steps/012_target/stdout.txt reports false !== true at dependent.test.ts:225 for the deep-recursive positive input. The verifier actually executes.

reference_support.evidence: verifier_reference/repeat_01 passes the selected official test. However, agent_reference/repeat_01/steps/009_target/stdout.txt reports RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded in recursive alias/composition resolution for the unchanged original agent test.

notes: The selected official defect is supported independently; reference failure on another legitimate recursive schema does not erase that defect.
The original t is P PASS / R FAIL and therefore Not Comparable/Unresolved for the required context-recovery contrast with this reference.
Do not repair the official solution or remove allOf/change the schema to manufacture original-t PASS/PASS; those alter the reference or stimulus.
A later review needs a principled comparable reference if this original test is retained. Repeating the already reproduced stack overflow is not the missing semantic evidence.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The instruction says scoped containers initialize independently and parent singletons are not reinitialized. Official tests/test.patch:354-381 additionally requires a never-initialized parent singleton to remain uninitialized after child.initialize(). The delivered implementation initializes it once through the child and does not repeat it at parent.initialize(). 'Not reinitialized' does not explicitly prohibit this first initialization. The stronger ownership/timing requirement is not unambiguously established by the supplied task text.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: screening/S011/agent_selected.test.ts directly tests scope.initialize(), asserting runs == 1, root resolution, and no second initialization at root.initialize(). Trajectory steps 95/99/103 explicitly list the selected test PASS and step 115 reconfirms all 24 tests. Fresh delivered selected test passes.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: cases/S011/baseline/verifier_delivered/repeat_01/steps/012_target/stderr.txt reports initOrder ['parentSingleton','scoped'] instead of ['scoped']. This is an executed observable ordering/state difference. Whether it violates the intended request remains unresolved.

reference_support.evidence: verifier_reference/repeat_01 passes. agent_reference/repeat_01/steps/009_target/stderr.txt fails the original runs == 1 assertion, receiving 0. The official reference implements the stricter interpretation but does not remove the task-text ambiguity.

notes: Needed evidence: an independent, pre-existing rule that scope initialization must exclude never-initialized parent-owned singletons, not merely avoid running them twice.
Do not call this Assertion Repair Required as a confirmed task miss until the contract dispute is settled.
Even under the official interpretation, this original t has P PASS / R FAIL; reversing runs == 1 or deleting root metrics assertions changes the oracle.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The instruction requires JSON metrics/cache_info and warm-cache with exit 0 and empty results. With explicit '-f json', empty results can be represented by results:[], while an empty stdout is not JSON and cannot include the required JSON sections. model.patch:245-246 exits before the normal reporting path for every warm-cache run.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: The original IncrementalTests.test_warm_cache invokes warm-cache with '-f json', checks exit 0, asserts stdout == b'', and then checks the populated cache summary. Trajectory step 53 reports the containing 25 tests passed. Fresh agent_delivered/repeat_01 passes.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: cases/S015/baseline/verifier_delivered/repeat_01/steps/012_target/stdout.txt reports JSONDecodeError on json.loads(result.stdout), with s == ''. The CLI has executed; this is malformed requested output, not infrastructure failure.

reference_support.evidence: verifier_reference/repeat_01 passes. agent_reference/repeat_01/steps/009_target/stdout.txt fails the byte-empty assertion and shows valid JSON with cache_info, metrics, errors:[], and results:[].

notes: Warm-cache's no-issues requirement is compatible with JSON output; it does not require all output to disappear.
The chosen original oracle affirmatively expects the malformed JSON behavior. It is P PASS / R FAIL; parsing stdout and asserting results == [] would be Assertion Repair Required.

Changing format flags, capturing a different stream, or redirecting output to satisfy the byte-empty assertion changes the stimulus or observation, rather than recovering the same validation by setup.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The task explicitly makes suppressions statement-wide when any physical line of a multiline statement is suppressed. tests/test.patch:254-258 (test_058_region_unioned_across_statement_lines) begins B602 suppression within a multiline Popen call and explicitly ends it after the call. A B602 finding remains on the delivered patch although the closing line is in that region.

Trajectory step 78 reports 81 functional tests OK and step 144 reports 319 tests OK. Fresh agent_delivered and agent_reference selected tests both report OK.

This selected defect is observable unsuppressed output rather than a disputed metric category.

reference_support.evidence: verifier_statement_wide_reference/repeat_01/steps/012_target/stdout.txt reports OK; the original agent fixture test also passes on reference.

notes: Use test_058 as the eligibility anchor. test_071's specific-versus-blanket metric expectation is not needed for this judgment.

The fixed target is the original fixture analysis with its exact fixture contents and aggregate assertions. Rewriting the Popen into multiline form, moving directives inside its statement, or changing expected counts changes stimulus/assertions, not preceding setup.
The original t has P/R PASS/PASS. A setup-only exposure and target-mechanism audit are still required before calling this context-recoverable.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: Required behaviors 10 and 11 say jobs spawned under a handle inherit it and are skipped if that handle is cancelled before starting. tests/test.patch:139 onward schedules a Promise.resolve().then side effect inside Script::evaluate_with_evaluation, later cancels that handle, and drains the queue. The archived run observes sessionTick == 1 instead of 0.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: screening/S022/agent_selected.rs enqueues a GenericJob through a native callback while eval_with_evaluation is active, cancels the handle, calls run_jobs(), and asserts its flag stays false. Original trajectory step 98 explicitly reports this test ok; steps 132 and 161 reconfirm it. Fresh agent_delivered/repeat_01_retry_03/steps/009_target/stdout.txt reports 1 passed.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: Archived test-stdout.txt:96-115 shows an executed cancelled_session_jobs_are_skipped_but_unrelated_jobs_still_run panic: cancelled session jobs must not execute, left 1, right 0. Sixteen other official tests pass. Fresh selected verifier execution was not yet available at the final evidence check.

reference_support.evidence: Official solution.patch associates evaluation state inside JobExecutor::enqueue_job for all job variants, including PromiseJob (approximately lines 460-487). This supports the intended mechanism statically. Fresh original-agent reference and official-verifier P/R baselines were not yet present at the final check.

notes: Needed evidence: completed fresh original-t P/R and official-verifier P/R raw results; at review time only one delivered original-t target result was present.

The agent's selected observation is a GenericJob callback flag, whereas the first official failure is a JavaScript Promise reaction side effect. Replacing GenericJob with PromiseJob or changing the evaluated script to schedule a Promise is a stimulus change unless independently justified as preceding setup while preserving the original target and assertion.

A setup that merely makes eval_with_evaluation fail before its callback runs would be target bypass only after the full allowed contrast is established; a new setup assertion is not itself evidence of recovery.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The instruction explicitly requires refine to fix failed fields while preserving structured fields. model.patch:286-296 merges all replacement data over original data. Official TestRefine.test_preserves_successful_fields observes previously successful a=1 overwritten by a=999.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: Original test_refine_new_data_takes_precedence structures x=1, refines with x=100 and y='hello', and asserts A(100,'hello'). Trajectory step 111 updates that test and reports 21 passed; step 124 reconfirms 21 passed. Fresh delivered selected test passes.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: cases/S023/baseline/delivered_verifier_r1/steps/012_target/stdout.txt reports refined.value.a == 999 while expected 1. This directly contradicts the preservation requirement.

reference_support.evidence: reference_verifier_r1/steps/012_target/stdout.txt passes. reference_agent_r1/steps/009_target/stdout.txt fails A(100,'hello') because the preserved value is A(1,'hello'), consistent with the task. Official solution.patch:83-90 uses only failed-field replacement data.

notes: This is an agent oracle accepting a task violation, not merely an unexercised edge case.
The original t is P PASS / R FAIL. Changing expected x=100 to x=1 is Assertion Repair Required.

Changing initial x into a failed field to make both implementations accept its replacement changes the target's semantic precondition and should not be silently treated as the same preservation test. Any such setup must be explicitly audited for whether it removes the disputed behavior.

task_contract_support_for_verifier_defec.evidence: The instruction requires starting any new fetch to abort the previous signal. The constructor uses #runFetch('', {immediate:true}) at model.patch:222-224, which stores its controller. However, #handleFetchSuccess clears #controller at model.patch:392-396; #invalidateFetch only aborts a retained controller at lines 554-558. Official test checks previous signals after prior fetches have settled (50ms resolver, 1000ms flushes), exposing this loss of the controller on completion.

agent_test_relevance.evidence: The original 'only latest fetch result is applied and previous signal is aborted' test emits search 'a', records that call's signal, emits 'ab', asserts that recorded signal is aborted, resolves stale a, and checks latest filteredOptions. Trajectory step 63 authors the test; step 100 reports all 32 tests passed and step 111 the final suite passed. Both fresh delivered_agent_r1 and reference_agent_r1 selected tests pass.

verifier_is_actual_behavior_failure.evidence: cases/S025/baseline/delivered_verifier_r1/steps/013_target/stdout.txt and stderr.txt report previous AbortController is aborted when new fetch starts failing at expect(sig.aborted).toBe(true): false instead of true. The test runs real async resolver/timer interactions.

reference_support.evidence: reference_verifier_r1/steps/013_target/stdout.txt passes. Official solution.patch:220-225 retains the initial controller and uses its signal for the detection/first fetch. Original selected test P/R also passes.

notes: The original assertion observes a later a-search signal, while the verifier observes both constructor and a-search signals after completion. This difference must stay visible in the alignment description.

Frozen target/input/assertion must retain the original userInput events, timings, stale resolution, and asserted object identity. Replacing signals[0] with a different fetch's signal can change the observation/oracle even if the assertion text is unchanged.

A legitimate setup-only state/history intervention remains possible in principle, but needs an explicit identity and provenance audit plus the full P/R contrast. No recovery or masking/bypass claim is made here.

review_amendments.reason: Full source-path and raw postcheck review corrected an initial mistaken attribution from a partial patch snippet. The unretained temporary controller in #onSearchChange's synchronous-to-async branch is not the constructor path used here. This case's supported mechanism is #handleFetchSuccess discarding the controller after completion. Step 1 inclusion remains unchanged.
